chapter_name: Social Structure, Stratification and Social Processes in Society
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how society is organized into structures and layers, and explore the continuous processes of cooperation, competition, and conflict that keep society moving.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Social structure refers to the regular, predictable patterns of social interaction and behavior. Just like a building has a structure (walls, pillars), society is built on institutions like family, religion, and economy.

The division of society into different layers (strata) based on wealth, power, and prestige. It represents structured inequalities between different groups of people (like the caste system or class system).

A social process where individuals or groups work together towards a common goal. Karl Marx argued that in a capitalist society, cooperation is often forced (workers cooperating in a factory to survive).

A universal process in modern societies where individuals try to maximize their own advantage or reward. Capitalism heavily promotes competition, treating it as natural, but sociologists argue it is socially constructed.
When groups clash over scarce resources, power, or values. Conflict is an integral part of society and can lead to social change. It often arises from the inequalities created by stratification.

fun_activity.title: 🥞 The Stratification Cake
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a 3-layer cake. Label the top, middle, and bottom layers with different social classes (Upper, Middle, Lower). Write one advantage the top layer has that the bottom layer doesn't. This is social stratification!

exam_tips: 📌 Always explain that social structure is dynamic, not static. Human actions recreate the structure every day.
📌 Differentiate between 'Cooperation' (working for a shared goal) and 'Competition' (working to beat others to a goal).
📌 Remember that conflict does not always mean violence; it can be ideological, economic, or political.
quick_recap: ⭐ Emile Durkheim emphasized solidarity and cooperation as the glue that holds society together.
⭐ Karl Marx focused on conflict, believing that society is fundamentally divided into opposing classes.
⭐ Stratification passes inequalities from one generation to the next, making social mobility difficult for those at the bottom.
